title: Relative Proj is invariant under tensoring by an invertible module
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal E$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $n\ge0$. There is a canonical isomorphism over $S$ between the projective bundles $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$ and $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, commuting with their structure morphisms to $S$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism; def-nagata-relative-proj].

source.place: Lemma Tag 02NC (constructions-lemma-twisting-and-proj), canonical relative-Proj isomorphism for the graded twist

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E'=\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, with $\mathcal L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_S$. By [def-sc-invertible-module] choose local generators $e_i$ of $\mathcal L$ on an open cover; refine to affine opens $U_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives inverse module maps $\tau_i:\mathcal E|_{U_i}\to\mathcal E'|_{U_i}$, $v\mapsto v\otimes e_i^{\otimes n}$, and $v\otimes a e_i^{\otimes n}\mapsto av$. For $n=0$ these are the unit identifications. In particular $\mathcal E'$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type: near any point these maps identify it with $\mathcal E$, so the affine module presentation and the finite generating surjection in [pqf-def-coherent] also present $\mathcal E'$.

source.place: Tag 02NC, label lemma-twisting-and-proj, proof: trivialize the invertible module and glue; specialization to the symmetric algebra and the tensor power of the line bundle

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E')$. The sheaf symmetric-algebra theorem [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] supplies these quasi-coherent algebras and their functoriality. Applying its universal property to $\tau_i$ and $\tau_i^{-1}$ gives inverse algebra maps $\beta_i:\mathcal A|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B|_{U_i}$: each composite fixes the degree-one generators, hence is the identity by uniqueness. The monomial description of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] makes these maps degree preserving and the identity in degree zero. On any affine $V\subseteq U_i$ they are graded $R$-algebra isomorphisms $A\to B$, where $R=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_S)$, $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal B)$; the affine-section clause of the sheaf symmetric-algebra theorem identifies these with the ordinary symmetric algebras and their symmetric gradings.

source.place: Tags 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra), 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence); symmetric-algebra construction used in constructions.tex Tag 02NC (lemma-twisting-and-proj)

proof.text:
Here is the local isomorphism induced by any $\beta_i:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ of step 2. Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with both base rings equal to $R$ and the identity $R\to R$, so that $R\otimes_RA=A$, and with the graded $R$-algebra isomorphism $\beta_i$ (both unit maps land in degree zero by step 2). It gives a canonical morphism $r_{\beta_i}:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ such that, for $f\in A_d$ with $d>0$, the inverse image of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\beta_i(f))$, and on it $r_{\beta_i}$ is the spectrum morphism of
$$A_{(f),0}\longrightarrow B_{(\beta_i(f)),0},\qquad a/f^m\longmapsto\beta_i(a)/\beta_i(f)^m\quad(a\in A_{md})$$
[def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. These opens cover $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$, and the chart formulas determine $r_{\beta_i}$ uniquely. No non-zero-divisor hypothesis on $f$ is used.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj) with identity base map and Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), property (2), explicit degree-zero chart map; Tag 02NC (lemma-twisting-and-proj), local trivial case

proof.text: Applying the same lemma to $\beta_i^{-1}$ gives $r_{\beta_i^{-1}}:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. On every chart, each composite $r_{\beta_i}\circ r_{\beta_i^{-1}}$ or $r_{\beta_i^{-1}}\circ r_{\beta_i}$ is the spectrum morphism of the composite fraction map, i.e. of the identity map $a/f^m\mapsto a/f^m$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These chart opens cover, so both composites are identities by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Hence $r_{\beta_i}$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. For $V=U_i$, the affine restriction isomorphisms $i_{U_i}$ in [def-nagata-relative-proj] for $\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E$ and $\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E'$ thus give an isomorphism $g_i:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E')|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)|_{U_i}$ over $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), uniqueness of the chart-determined morphism; Tag 02NC (lemma-twisting-and-proj), local trivial case: the identity when L is trivial

proof.text:
Check a change of generator on any affine $W\subseteq U_i\cap U_j$. Write $e_j=u e_i$ with $u\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_S)^\times$; the inverse scalar comes from the inverse change of the two rank-one frames [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $\tau_j=u^n\tau_i$. Since a homogeneous degree-$k$ element is a sum of degree-$k$ monomials [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], $\beta_j(a)=u^{nk}\beta_i(a)$ for $a\in A_k$. Thus $D_+(\beta_j(f))=D_+(\beta_i(f))$ and on each such chart the two ring maps in step 3 satisfy
$$\frac{\beta_j(a)}{\beta_j(f)^m}=\frac{u^{nmd}\beta_i(a)}{(u^{nd}\beta_i(f))^m}=\frac{\beta_i(a)}{\beta_i(f)^m}\qquad(a\in A_{md}).$$
The equality only cancels powers of the unit $u$, using the localization fractions of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]; it does not cancel $f$. For $n=0$ both powers are $1$.

source.place: Tag 02NC, label lemma-twisting-and-proj, proof: trivialize the invertible module and glue; specialization to the symmetric algebra and the tensor power of the line bundle

proof.text: The same local formulas respect restrictions of the affine base. For an affine $V\subseteq U_i$, the module map sends $v$ to $v\otimes(e_i|_V)^{\otimes n}$; this is the restriction of $\tau_i$. Its symmetric-algebra map therefore restricts $\beta_i$ by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. On Proj charts, coefficient restriction $\rho$ sends $\beta_i(a)/\beta_i(f)^m$ to $\rho\beta_i(a)/\rho\beta_i(f)^m$, equal to applying the restricted algebra map after restriction. This is exactly the compatibility with the restriction maps specified in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. It also holds for the inverse maps. Thus the restriction of $g_i$ to $V$ is the map constructed there from $e_i|_V$.

source.place: Tag 02NC, label lemma-twisting-and-proj, proof: trivialize the invertible module and glue; specialization to the symmetric algebra and the tensor power of the line bundle

proof.text: Cover each $U_i\cap U_j$ by affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Steps 5 and 6, equality of affine spectrum maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the covering by standard charts [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] show that $g_i$ and $g_j$ agree on each of these restrictions; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives agreement on the whole overlap. Apply that lemma to glue $g_i$ to $g:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E')\to\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$. Their inverses agree on the corresponding overlaps, so they glue too, and the two composites are identities by local uniqueness. The equality of the structure morphisms holds locally because each $g_i$ is over $U_i$, hence globally by the same uniqueness. Any other cover and any other local generators compare on affine refinements by steps 5 and 6, so give the same $g$. Its inverse is the requested canonical isomorphism $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)\cong\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E')$ over $S$, with the projective-bundle meanings in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].
